title: Long-Held Payout Methods: Conversion Fee Discount, Questions Answered
content:
**What is the long-held method discount?** It is a discount on the conversion fee charged on a transfer to one of the host's Payout Methods paid in a currency other than USD, set by how long that payout method has been on file. The conversion fee's long-held method discount is 10% when the method's date added is at least 24 whole months before the settlement day, 5% when it is at least 12 but fewer than 24 whole months before it, and nothing for a newer method.

**Which date is read?** The date added on the payout method's own record, for the method the transfer was sent to. The date the host account was opened, and the dates of the host's other methods, are not read for this discount.

**Up to which day are the months counted?** To the settlement day of the transfer the fee belongs to, the day the conversion fee falls due: the rail's processing time in business days after the transfer was sent. Months are whole months.

**How do the bands look side by side?**

| Whole months from the method's date added to the settlement day | Long-held method discount |
|---|---|
| 24 or more | 10% |
| 12 to 23 | 5% |
| Fewer than 12 | Nothing |

**Where exactly are the lines?** With an imagined settlement day of 2026-05-12:

| Method added | Whole months | Discount |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-05-12 | 24 | 10% |
| 2024-05-13 | 23 | 5% |
| 2025-05-12 | 12 | 5% |
| 2025-05-13 | 11 | Nothing |

**Does re-verifying a method after a hold restart the count?** No. The count runs from the date the method was added, not from its verification date.
